42862275.label: Background
42862275.text: Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) is a critical biomarker for immunotherapy selection in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). However, the relationships between PD-L1 expression and non-invasive indicators, such as metabolic parameters derived from 18F-FDG PET/CT and never-smoker/never- or minimally-drinker (NSND) history, remain poorly defined. Moreover, whether these associations differ across nodal subgroups has not been investigated.

42862275.label: Methods
42862275.text: This retrospective study included 147 patients with resected OSCC who underwent preoperative PET/CT. Factors associated with high PD-L1 expression (combined positive score [CPS] ≥ 20) were assessed using logistic regression in the overall cohort and with subgroup analyses stratified by nodal status and formal interaction testing.

42862275.label: Results
42862275.text: In the overall cohort, maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) (odds ratio [OR] per unit increase = 1.067; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.013-1.123; P = 0.014) and gender (OR = 2.254; 95% CI: 1.029-4.936; P = 0.042) were independently associated with high PD-L1 expression. After stratification by nodal status, no clinicopathological or metabolic variable was significantly associated with PD-L1 expression in pN0 patients. In contrast, among pN+ patients, SUVmax (OR per unit increase = 1.113; 95% CI: 1.015-1.222; P = 0.024) and NSND (OR = 4.127; 95% CI: 1.362-12.501; P = 0.012) emerged as independent predictors. The NSND × pN interaction was significant (P = 0.004), whereas the SUVmax × pN interaction was not (P = 0.225).

42862275.label: Conclusions
42862275.text: SUVmax may serve as a candidate non-invasive indicator, whereas the association between NSND and high PD-L1 expression was modified by nodal status, with a significant effect in node-positive patients. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require external validation.

42867375.text: Background The clinical utility of quantitative T1 mapping in cardiac MRI is constrained by variability across acquisition protocols, and a comprehensive comparison between commonly used sequences remains unavailable. Purpose To provide a full range of cardiac MRI native T1 and extracellular volume fraction (ECV) values at 3 T in healthy Chinese adults and participants with various cardiovascular diseases and, as a secondary aim, to establish the relationship between modified Look-Locker inversion recovery (MOLLI) and shortened MOLLI (ShMOLLI) measurements. Materials and Methods This prospective study included healthy volunteers, participants with normal cardiac MRI findings, and participants representing 13 cardiovascular conditions. All participants underwent 3-T cardiac MRI with both MOLLI and ShMOLLI sequences during a single examination. Global native T1 and ECV values were quantified and compared between sequences and across disease groups. Statistical approaches included t tests, Pearson correlation, Bland-Altman analysis, and Cohen D standardization. Results This study included 1237 clinical participants (mean age ± SD: 51 years ± 14.8; 854 men). Reference values (adjusted mean ± SE) in healthy volunteers were 1170 msec ± 9 (MOLLI) and 1135 msec ± 10 (ShMOLLI) for native T1 and were 24.8% ± 0.6 (both MOLLI and ShMOLLI) for ECV, with women showing higher native T1 values than men (all P ≤ .002). MOLLI yielded systematically higher native T1 than ShMOLLI across all conditions (mean difference: 46.0 msec ± 27.2; all P < .01), whereas ECV did not differ for most conditions (10 of 15 groups; P > .05). Strong intersequence correlations were observed for native T1 (Pearson r = 0.93; P < .001) and ECV (r = 0.95; P < .001). After standardization to sequence-specific baselines, pathologic deviations were comparable between sequences (Cohen D differences ≤0.5 in most groups). A supplementary swine study supported the technical validity of both sequences (r = 0.87-0.90; P < .001). Conclusion In participants who underwent 3-T cardiac MRI with both MOLLI and ShMOLLI sequences, native T1 was higher with MOLLI than ShMOLLI, but ECV was consistent across sequences.

42912575.label: Background
42912575.text: Hyperkinetic biliary dyskinesia, defined as a gallbladder ejection fraction (EF) ≥80% on cholecystokinin (CCK)-stimulated hepatobiliary iminodiacetic acid scans in the setting of biliary-type pain, has been increasingly recognized as a potential functional gallbladder disorder. The clinical significance of this entity and the role of cholecystectomy remain uncertain.

42912575.label: Patients and methods
42912575.text: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies reporting outcomes in patients with CCK-hepatobiliary iminodiacetic acid EF ≥80% who underwent cholecystectomy due to non-acute biliary-type pain. Primary outcomes included mean EF, rates of symptom resolution and improvement following cholecystectomy, and prevalence of chronic cholecystitis on pathology. Secondary outcomes included normal histology rates and symptom reproduction with CCK stimulation. All statistical analyses were conducted in R (version 4.5.0) using a random-effects model to obtain pooled estimates.

42912575.label: Results
42912575.text: A total of 14 retrospective studies, including 686 patients, were analyzed. The pooled mean gallbladder EF was 90.27% (95% CI: 88.73-91.80, I 2 = 86.6%). Symptom resolution occurred in 83.1% (95% CI: 76.7-89.4, I 2 = 76.8%), and symptom improvement in 91.6% (95% CI: 89.0-94.2, I 2 = 29.7%) of patients following cholecystectomy. Histopathologic analysis revealed chronic cholecystitis in 85.1% (95% CI: 76.9-93.4, I 2 = 90.6%) of surgical specimens, while normal gallbladder histology was rare, observed in only 9.9% (95% CI: 4.6-15.2, I 2 = 83.7%). The pooled risk ratio indicated a 6.70-fold higher likelihood of chronic cholecystitis compared with normal histology (95% CI: 3.69-12.17, I 2 = 65.2%, P = 0.0022). Functional reproduction of symptoms during CCK stimulation was frequent, with a pooled rate of 78.3% (95% CI: 70.4-86.3, I 2 = 35.6%). Egger regression test suggested potential publication bias for the normal histology outcome ( P = 0.0223), but not for symptom resolution ( P = 0.1589).

42912575.label: Conclusions
42912575.text: This meta-analysis suggests that a high gallbladder EF in the setting of biliary-type pain could represent clinically relevant hyperkinetic biliary dyskinesia rather than normal physiology. Cholecystectomy appears to provide meaningful symptom relief in appropriately selected patients, and pathologic findings frequently indicate underlying chronic inflammation. Further studies are needed to establish clear diagnostic cutoffs and guide management.

42948875.text: Left atrial appendage closure is an increasingly used stroke prevention therapy for patients with atrial fibrillation who are unable to maintain long-term anticoagulation. Imaging quality and consistency are central to procedural safety and long-term outcomes, yet practice varies widely across centers. This review presents a practical, phase-based multimodality imaging framework intended to provide guidance and minimum standards for image acquisition and interpretation across all phases of left atrial appendage closure care, including preprocedural planning and thrombus exclusion, intraprocedural guidance and complication detection, and postprocedural surveillance for device-related thrombus and peridevice leak. Because sizing rules, sealing mechanisms, and leak patterns differ between the 2 contemporary platforms, device-specific considerations for the Watchman and Amulet systems are addressed throughout. Transesophageal echocardiography remains the reference standard for thrombus detection and procedural guidance, while cardiac computed tomography offers high spatial resolution, detailed 3-dimensional characterization, and complementary leak assessment, with optimal modality selection influenced by patient characteristics, operator expertise, and institutional resources. Intracardiac echocardiography and mini transesophageal echocardiographic support anesthesia-sparing workflows. Standardized device-related thrombus and peridevice leak classification and harmonized imaging protocols can enhance reproducibility and facilitate cross-center comparisons. Emerging technologies including computed tomography first workflows, 4-dimensional imaging, AI applications, and computational modeling further advance precision planning and surveillance.

42950525.label: Objective
42950525.text: To evaluate an optimized CT enterography (CTE) strategy combining reduced radiation exposure and iodine administration in patients with Crohn's disease (CD), with subjective image quality as the primary endpoint.

42950525.label: Methods
42950525.text: This prospective single-center randomized study enrolled 102 patients with CD who underwent CTE between February and October 2025. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio using a computer-generated random sequence, with allocation concealed in sequentially numbered, opaque, sealed envelopes opened by a research nurse not involved in patient enrollment, image evaluation, or clinical data collection. No stratification or blocking was used. The three protocols were: a standard-dose protocol (Group A), a low-dose protocol using 100 kVp and 70% adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction-V (ASIR-V) (Group B), and a combined low-dose, low-contrast protocol using the same acquisition settings with a reduced iodine dose (320 mgI/kg, corresponding to 1.0 mL/kg of contrast medium) (Group C). The primary endpoint was subjective image quality assessed using a 5-point Likert scale. Secondary endpoints included objective image quality, bowel wall enhancement, and radiation dose metrics. Diagnostic performance for disease activity and luminal stenosis was evaluated as an exploratory analysis in patients with an eligible endoscopic reference standard; the study was not designed or powered for diagnostic non-inferiority or equivalence testing.

42950525.label: Results
42950525.text: No statistically significant between-group differences were detected in baseline characteristics (all p > 0.05). For the primary endpoint, mean subjective image quality scores were 4.3 ± 0.5, 4.5 ± 0.6, and 4.5 ± 0.5 in Groups A, B, and C, respectively, with no significant between-group difference (p = 0.27); the between-group differences were 0.2 points (95% CI, -0.1 to 0.5) for Group B versus A, 0.2 points (95% CI, -0.1 to 0.5) for Group C versus A, and 0.0 points (95% CI, -0.3 to 0.3) for Group C versus B. Compared with the standard protocol, the estimated effective radiation dose was reduced by 53.2% in Group B and 50.0% in Group C (both p < 0.001), with no significant difference between the two optimized protocols. Both optimized protocols showed lower image noise and higher signal-to-noise and contrast-to-noise ratios than the standard protocol (all p < 0.05), whereas no statistically significant between-group differences were detected in bowel wall attenuation (all p > 0.05). For the exploratory diagnostic analysis, 76/102 patients had an eligible endoscopic reference standard (Group A, 25/31; Group B, 28/38; Group C, 23/33). Diagnostic accuracy for disease activity was 88.0% (95% CI, 70.0-95.8%) in Group A, 89.3% (95% CI, 72.8-96.3%) in Group B, and 87.0% (95% CI, 67.9-95.5%) in Group C; the corresponding between-group differences were 1.3 percentage points (95% CI, -16.8 to 19.4) for B versus A, -1.0 percentage points (95% CI, -19.4 to 17.4) for C versus A, and 2.3 percentage points (95% CI, -16.6 to 21.2) for B versus C. For luminal stenosis, diagnostic accuracy was 84.0% (95% CI, 65.3-94.1%), 89.3% (95% CI, 72.8-96.3%), and 87.0% (95% CI, 67.9-95.5%), respectively; the absolute differences were 5.3 percentage points (95% CI, -12.1 to 22.7) for B versus A, 3.0 percentage points (95% CI, -15.2 to 21.2) for C versus A, and 2.3 percentage points (95% CI, -16.6 to 21.2) for B versus C. The confidence intervals for between-group differences were wide and included values that could be clinically relevant; because the study was not powered to establish diagnostic non-inferiority or equivalence, the absence of statistically significant differences should not be interpreted as evidence of diagnostic equivalence or non-inferiority.

42950525.label: Conclusion
42950525.text: On the GE Revolution 256-detector-row CT platform, the optimized CTE protocols reduced radiation exposure by approximately 50%, while Group C additionally achieved a protocol-defined 33.3% reduction in weight-normalized iodine dose. Based on the observed dose and image-quality findings, Group B can reasonably be recommended when radiation reduction is the primary goal, whereas Group C may be considered when both radiation and iodine reduction are desired. These findings do not establish equivalence or non-inferiority in image quality or diagnostic performance.

43008425.label: Background
43008425.text: PI-RADS scoring of transition zone (TZ) lesions is strongly reader-dependent, particularly in the PI-RADS 4 category. We compared diagnostic performance and inter-reader agreement between a specialized high-volume center and non-specialized referring centers.

43008425.label: Methods
43008425.text: Overall, 315 men with a TZ lesion scored PI-RADS ≥ 3 underwent MRI-guided in-bore biopsy and were stratified by interpreting site (non-specialized vs specialized). The erased-margins criterion was reassessed centrally by one specialized-center reader (the biopsy operator) and, in a 125-lesion subset, by three independent readers.

43008425.label: Results
43008425.text: Positive predictive value for clinically significant cancer (csPCa, Grade Group ≥ 2) at PI-RADS ≥ 4 was higher in the specialized cohort (43.3% vs 29.5%, p = 0.015). For PI-RADS 4 lesions, detection of any cancer was 76.9% vs 42.6% (p < 0.001), but not significantly different for csPCa (32.1% vs 22.8%, p = 0.16). On central reassessment, non-specialized centers had more often assigned PI-RADS 4 to lesions without erased margins (50% vs 35%, p = 0.048), a difference not replicated by the three independent readers. Agreement on PI-RADS category was substantial within and moderate between centers (κ 0.68 vs 0.43-0.49); agreement on the erased-margins criterion was fair-to-moderate (Fleiss κ 0.30), and its discriminative value decreased with decreasing expertise (AUC 0.82, 0.75, 0.70), largely reflecting lesion identification. The central reassessment did not outperform blinded readers (AUC 0.69).

43008425.label: Conclusion
43008425.text: Specialized interpretation was associated with higher diagnostic yield for TZ lesions, particularly PI-RADS 4. Reader-dependent application of the erased-margins criterion is a candidate mechanism requiring confirmation and a potential training target rather than a stand-alone rule; prospective external validation is needed.

43052075.label: Background
43052075.text: Invasive myocardial perfusion normalizes absolute coronary flow to subtended myocardial mass. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) assigns vessel-specific mass using a Voronoi algorithm, whereas echocardiography incorporates wall thickness into total left ventricular (LV) mass. Their impact in left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) is uncertain.

43052075.label: Methods
43052075.text: We included 219 patients undergoing continuous thermodilution assessment in the left anterior descending artery (LAD) with available transthoracic echocardiography and CCTA. Absolute coronary flow (Q, mL/min) was measured at rest and during hyperaemia. The LAD territorial percentage was derived from CCTA using the Voronoi algorithm. LAD-subtended mass was calculated as this percentage multiplied by total LV mass obtained from either CCTA or echocardiography. Myocardial perfusion (MP mL/min/g) was calculated as Q divided by LAD-subtended mass, generating MPLAD,CT and MPLAD, Echo, and compared across LV geometry phenotypes.

43052075.label: Results
43052075.text: Echocardiographic and CCTA-derived total LV mass correlated moderately (r = 0.65, p < 0.001), but echocardiography yielded higher values (mean bias 30 g), with greater divergence in LVH. Concentric and eccentric LVH independently predicted discrepancy. In patients without LVH, perfusion was similar (rest: 1.12 vs 1.05 mL/min/g, p = 0.137; hyperaemia: 3.03 vs 2.62 mL/min/g, p = 0.057). In concentric LVH, MPLAD,CT was higher than MPLAD, Echo (rest: 1.14 vs 0.71; hyperaemia: 2.55 vs 1.46 mL/min/g; both p < 0.001). Similar differences occurred in eccentric LVH (rest: 0.81 vs 0.63; hyperaemia: 2.00 vs 1.54 mL/min/g; both p < 0.001).

43052075.label: Conclusions
43052075.text: Myocardial mass methodology significantly influences invasive perfusion. In LVH, particularly concentric hypertrophy, CCTA- and echocardiography-based mass estimation diverge, resulting in substantial differences in calculated perfusion. Mass-independent indices may provide more robust assessment.

43062625.label: Objective
43062625.text: Radium-223 dichloride (Ra-223) prolongs overall survival in castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) with symptomatic bone metastases, but the ERA-223 trial reported an increased fracture rate when Ra-223 was combined with an androgen receptor signaling inhibitor (ARSI), and concurrent use of a bone-modifying agent (BMA) attenuated this risk. Few studies have quantitatively characterized real-world concurrent BMA use during Ra-223 treatment in Asia, or examined its association with fracture risk with competing risks taken into account. This study aimed to describe the real-world rate of concurrent BMA use during Ra-223 treatment in Japan and to quantify its association with fracture risk.

43062625.label: Methods
43062625.text: In this retrospective observational study using the DeSC Database, a Japanese administrative claims database, 1,132 patients with a claim for Ra-223 were identified, and the date of the first claim was defined as day 0. After excluding patients with less than one year of prior observation, patients with another primary cancer, and patients who had a fracture diagnosis or the competing event of death, or whose observation ended, during the 8 weeks after day 0, the analysis set comprised 538 patients. Concurrent BMA use was defined by a claim for denosumab or zoledronic acid during the 8 weeks after day 0. The primary outcome was any fracture, identified from fracture diagnosis codes recorded after the landmark. Cumulative incidence was estimated with death as a competing event, and multivariable Fine-Gray regression and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) were applied.

43062625.label: Results
43062625.text: Concurrent BMA use was present in 250 patients (46.5%). Any fracture occurred in 91 patients, with a cumulative incidence of 14.1% at 12 months and 19.0% at 24 months after the landmark. Concurrent BMA use was associated with a lower fracture risk (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR] 0.26, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.16-0.42), whereas concurrent ARSI use (sHR 2.18, 95% CI 1.40-3.40) and a history of fracture diagnosis (sHR 2.55, 95% CI 1.32-4.92) were associated with increased risk. The IPTW analysis was concordant (sHR 0.29, 95% CI 0.18-0.47).

43062625.label: Conclusions
43062625.text: Concurrent BMA use during Ra-223 treatment remained below half in Japanese real-world practice, yet was associated with a substantially lower fracture risk under competing risks.

43076675.text: Background Hourglass-like constrictions (HGCs) of peripheral nerves are hallmark findings of Parsonage-Turner syndrome (PTS), but their longitudinal characteristics and associations with motor strength and electromyography (EMG) findings, as well as their prognostic value, are unknown. Purpose To delineate longitudinal changes of HGCs and muscle edema with MR neurography (MRN) and to determine their associations with outcomes. Materials and Methods In this prospective study (July 2020 to January 2024), individuals diagnosed with PTS less than 6 months from symptom onset with EMG-confirmed muscle denervation underwent longitudinal assessments (baseline and 3, 6, and 12 months) with physical examination (for muscle strength), EMG, participant-reported outcomes, and 3-T MRN. Two readers independently counted severe and mild HGCs and graded the degree of muscle edema as "severe," "moderate," "mild," or "none." Associations of MRN findings and days from symptom onset with EMG findings and muscle strength were evaluated. Logistic and linear regression analyses were performed to assess whether baseline MRN findings were predictive of follow-up outcomes. Results Among 45 participants (median age, 47.2 years [IQR, 38.7-57.3 years]; 27 male), analyses included 58 affected nerves and 112 affected muscles. Most nerves (90% [52 of 58]) demonstrated HGCs and a median of one to two severe HGCs at baseline, which reduced in frequency (78%-82% [35-37 of 45]) and severity (zero to one) at 12 months. Muscle edema was graded moderate on average at baseline and reduced to mild at 12 months. HGCs were not associated with EMG findings or muscle strength, but a more severe muscle edema grade was associated with increased EMG denervation (odds ratio, 3.19-13.9). HGCs and muscle edema at baseline were not predictive of outcomes, except for muscle edema prediction of self-reported disability at the 3- to 6-month follow-up (β = 4.7-5.9). Conclusion HGCs persisted over the course of 1-year follow-up in PTS but were neither independently predictive of nor associated with muscle strength recovery. Muscle edema grades were associated with EMG denervation.
